Thursday, September 3, 2026 Daily Digest

Adobe Acquires Rilo, Webflow Unveils Source, JetStream Ships Agent Governance

Today's top stories in AI + enterprise tech

1

Adobe Acquires Rilo to Build Agentic Marketing Workflows

Adobe acquired Rilo, an India-based AI startup that lets users describe marketing tasks in plain English and have AI agents execute them. The platform built workflows for competitive intelligence, content distribution, lead enrichment, and sales-call analysis — all orchestrated by coordinating agents. This is Adobe's second Indian AI acquisition after Rephrase.ai in 2023, and signals its push into the workflow automation layer that sits above content creation.

Read on CXO Voice →
2

Webflow Unveils "Source" — Agentic Workspace for Marketing Teams

At Webflow Conf 2026, the company launched Source — a platform giving marketing teams and AI agents shared, governed access to website code and martech stacks. Source bridges agentic and visual development, letting campaigns go from brief to live landing pages with personalized variants in hours. Webflow also unveiled Campaigns (for performance marketers) and Assets (for on-brand creative), plus tech from acquired startup Vidoso.

Read on CMSWire →
3

JetStream "Clearance" — Per-Action Authorization for AI Agents

JetStream debuted Clearance, a reasoning engine that evaluates and authorizes every agent action before it executes — blocking dangerous sequences like exfiltration patterns rather than logging them after the fact. For enterprises running large fleets of agents or customer-facing automation, this is a governance breakthrough: stop bad actions mid-sequence instead of relying on post-hoc detection.

Read on AI Agent Store →
4

Anthropic Ships Fable 5.1 and Gated Mythos 5.1 — Cache Reads 75% Cheaper

Anthropic released Fable 5.1 as its improved general-purpose agent model, plus a gated Mythos 5.1 for vetted defenders and researchers. Both feature a 1M-token context window and 75% reduction in prompt cache-read pricing. The cost cuts make long-running agent sessions practical — complex multi-hour workflows that maintain stateful memory are now economically viable for enterprise use.

Read on AI Agent Store →
5

Meta's $18B Settlement Clears Path for AI Product Pipeline

Morgan Stanley analysts say Meta's massive social media settlement lifts a legal overhang that may clear the way for new AI product launches — including MetaClaw, improved MetaAI, agentic ad tooling for SMBs, and the consumer AI agent "Hatch" (reportedly able to make purchases and bookings autonomously). The pattern: after Google's DOJ ruling, it launched Gemini 3 and AI Mode. Morgan Stanley expects Meta to follow suit.

Read on CNBC →

💡 My Take

Read this one: The JetStream "Clearance" announcement. The shift from "log then review" to "authorize before execute" is the governance model enterprise AI actually needs. As agents gain the ability to take real-world actions — send emails, move money, modify systems — pre-action authorization becomes non-negotiable. This is the pattern that will define trusted agentic deployments.
